new_issues.description: The Introduction says rural and income associations with timeliness 'point in different directions across studies [5, 6, 7]', but the cited studies, as the manuscript itself describes them, do not show opposing directions. [5] (Di Vanna) reports shorter intervals for lower-income and non-metropolitan patients, and [6] (Montiel Ishino) lower odds of delay in rural Appalachian counties, which is the same direction. [7] (Semprini) reports that the effect of hospital accreditation differs by county income, not an opposite income or rural direction. The claim motivating the direction-free design is left without citation support.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: Introduction "rural and income associations with timeliness point in different directions across studies [5, 6, 7]"
new_issues.competence_basis: Domain literature on prostate cancer time to treatment (Card #3). Checked against the manuscript's own descriptions of [5], [6] and [7] and against reports/phase1.md (Di Vanna 2025, Montiel Ishino 2021, Semprini 2026); full texts not read.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: Compared the same sentence in both manuscripts. The original cited [2, 7, 8] (Foley 2022 Tasmanian study, where remote men waited longer, plus Di Vanna and Montiel Ishino), which did contain an opposite direction. The revision replaced the Tasmanian citation with Semprini [7], leaving only same-direction or non-directional sources.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: REV-7 required removing the US-versus-Tasmanian directional juxtaposition, which the revision did. This issue is whether the replacement US citations support the 'different directions' claim, a citation-support defect that REV-7's criterion does not test.

new_issues.description: The supplement guide says Supplementary Table S35 (clinical-need increment in the prostatectomy-only scenario) comes from analyses specified under protocol amendment 1.9, and Methods say the 1.9 analyses were specified before being run. However, amendment 1.9 in Supplementary Table S43 lists items (a) to (h) without this analysis, and the Methods post-review paragraph does not mention it, so its specification status is undocumented.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: Supplementary material, How to read this supplement "Supplementary Tables S7, S11 to S15, S17, S18, S21, S22 and S35 come from analyses specified after an internal review (protocol amendment 1.9)"
new_issues.competence_basis: Analytic provenance and post hoc labelling (Card #2 focus on analytic choices made after seeing results). Compared the supplement guide, Methods post-review paragraph, S43 amendment 1.9 text and reports/phase4_revision.md, which presents this analysis as a separate section outside items (a) to (h).
new_issues.attribution_evidence: S35, the supplement guide sentence and amendment 1.9 exist only in the revised manuscript; the original had no such table or label.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: REV-35 asked for the prostatectomy-only clinical-need increment to appear in the main text, which it does. This issue concerns the undocumented pre-specification label attached to that new analysis, which no roadmap item covers.

new_issues.description: Under the new per-step tuning, penalised logistic regression chose C at the lower edge of the pre-specified grid (0.01) in 8 of 15 stratum and step combinations (all men at steps 0 to 2, low risk at steps 1 and 2, step 2 in intermediate, high and unknown risk). The wider-grid check was run only for the original step 3 tuning. The manuscript reports the grid edge only for the primary tuning and does not disclose these per-step edge choices.
new_issues.location_anchor: table: Supplementary Table S13 — penalised logistic regression C = 0.01 at step 2 in every stratum and at steps 0 and 1 in all men, the lowest value of the 0.01 to 10 grid
new_issues.competence_basis: Hyperparameter tuning and grid choices (Card #2 focus). Counted from S13 and confirmed against reports/phase4_revision.md summary ('C was chosen at an edge of the grid (0.01 or 10) in 8 of 15 stratum and step combinations'); impact on increments likely small given S34.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: Per-step tuning, S13 and the post-review paragraph exist only in the revised manuscript. The revised Results grid-edge sentence and Discussion refer to the step 3 tuning and the wider-grid check (S34), which the original also reported.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: REV-25 required per-step tuning, increments and a restricted model-comparison inference, all of which were delivered. This issue is an undisclosed grid-edge result inside that new tuning. REV-16 covers grid-edge disclosure only for the secondary outcome.

new_issues.description: The reference profile is described as 'a metropolitan county of 1 million or more', and the Results say 'metropolitan counties of 1 million or more'. The Rural-Urban Continuum Code category is counties in metropolitan areas of 1 million or more population, so the wording wrongly implies a county population threshold.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: Methods, Standardised percentages "living in a metropolitan county of 1 million or more"
new_issues.competence_basis: SEER county attribute coding (Card #3). Checked against the rurality labels in config/analysis.yaml ('Counties in metropolitan areas ge 1 million pop').
new_issues.attribution_evidence: The original Results, Cohort already read 'against 1.1% of men in metropolitan counties of 1 million or more', and the revised Results keep this wording, so the defect is present in both versions. The original Methods had the accurate 'a county in a metropolitan area of 1 million or more'; the revision carried the inaccurate form into Methods as well.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: REV-42 concerns 'corresponds to' wording in Supplementary Box 2 and calling US counties 'remote'. It does not cover the metropolitan-area population label of the Rural-Urban Continuum Code categories.
